Expense Claim — Edit

The Expense Claim form enables you to record and process reimbursement requests from employees, members, or other authorized persons who have incurred business expenses using their personal funds.

Use this form when individuals need reimbursement for out-of-pocket business expenses such as travel costs, client entertainment, office supplies, or professional development.

How Expense Claims Work

When you create an expense claim, the system records a liability showing what the business owes to the claimant.

This liability remains until you process the reimbursement through a Payment transaction.

Each expense line can be allocated to different accounts, projects, or tracking categories for accurate cost reporting.

Creating an Expense Claim

Start by selecting the person who incurred the expenses and enter the claim date.

Add line items for each expense, specifying the account, amount, and description.

Include relevant details such as merchant names, expense dates, and business purpose for each item.

Attach receipts or other supporting documents to validate the expenses.

Form Fields

Complete the following fields to create an expense claim:

Date

Basic Information

Enter the date of the expense claim. This is typically when the expenses were incurred or when the claim is submitted.

This date determines when the expenses are recorded in your accounts and when the liability to reimburse is recognized.

Reference

Enter a reference number for this expense claim. This helps track and process reimbursement requests.

You can use automatic numbering or create your own system, such as employee initials plus date.

Paid by

Claimant Details

Select the employee or capital account holder who paid for these expenses and should be reimbursed.

This creates a liability in your accounts showing you owe this person reimbursement for their out-of-pocket expenses.

Payee

Enter the name of the vendor or payee to whom the expenses were paid. This helps identify where the money was spent.

For example, enter the restaurant name for meal expenses or the taxi company for transportation costs.

Currency

Currency and Exchange Rate

Select the currency in which the expenses were paid if different from your base currency.

This is useful for travel expenses paid in foreign currencies that need to be reimbursed in your base currency.

Exchange rate

Enter the exchange rate for converting the foreign currency expenses to your base currency for reimbursement.

Use the exchange rate from when the expenses were incurred, not the current rate, for accurate cost recording.

Description

Optionally, add a description or notes about this expense claim, such as the purpose of the expenses or trip details.

Good descriptions help with approval processes and provide context for auditing and tax purposes.

Lines

Expense Line Items

Enter the individual expense items. Each line represents a different expense with its amount and account allocation.

Break down expenses by type (meals, transport, accommodation) and allocate to appropriate expense accounts.

Inventory Location

If any expenses are for inventory items, select the location where the inventory should be added.

This is used when employees purchase inventory items directly, such as emergency supplies or materials.

Amounts are tax inclusive

Check this box if the expense amounts already include tax. Leave unchecked if tax needs to be added.

Most receipts show tax-inclusive amounts, so this box is usually checked for expense claims.

Column — Description

Check this box to show a description column for each expense line, allowing detailed explanations of each expense.

Descriptions help explain the business purpose of each expense, which is important for tax deductibility.
